title: Weekly ops prioritization scratchpad - SRE
body:
Meeting: SRE weekly ops sync prep (aim: triage paging, prioritize 1-2 reliability actions, align on SLO/alert tuning)
Date: 2026-04-19 10:00am PT
Attendees (suggested): Priya, Ethan, Marta, Arjun, on-call SRE, representative from serving-runtime

Quick summary notes to self:
- High-level ask: pick 2 operational fixes we can commit to in next sprint that noticeably reduce pager noise or SLO burn.
- Bring concise metrics: pager volume trend (7d/30d), top alert sources, error budget % by service, p95 latency regressions.
- Flag customer-facing incidents that still need comms (make sure CS knows) and any rollbacks required.

Metrics snapshot (bring real dashboard links during meeting):
- Pager volume: ~42 pages last week (vs 28 w/w) — spike on Tue night.
- Top page sources: model-serving-timeouts (35%), kv-cache-evictions (25%), autoscaler-throttles (15%).
- SLO health: hosted-api write SLO burned 18% (30d window), embeddings SLO burned 5%, dedicated-serving p99 latency crossed threshold twice.
- Latency: text-gen p50 120ms (ok), p95 780ms (up from 620ms last week).

Initial hypotheses for the spike:
- Long-tail GC on older CUDA drivers caused occasional host stalls on a small pool of Dedicated nodes (see ENGINFRA-2345).
- KV cache eviction surge due to recent rollout of cache-key change in model routing (proto change).
- Autoscaler policy slightly more aggressive after config tweak; thrashing when load is spiky (scale-down too fast).

Top incidents to call out quickly (brief):
- Incident A (2026-04-14 02:10 UTC): Serving timeouts for r2-large in us-west-2. Scope: ~4 min blip, ~18 customer requests failed. RCA: degraded NVML metrics + driver stall on 3 nodes. Status: patch deployed, monitoring stable. Follow-up: schedule maintenance to update drivers on remaining nodes.
- Incident B (2026-04-16 17:40 UTC): KV eviction storm after model-routing rollout. Scope: increased tail latency for embeddings, correlated with cache-key change. RCA: key namespace collision + cache warming issue. Status: rollback to previous routing pushed; warming job in progress. Follow-up: add canary and cache-warm job to rollout checklist.
- Incident C (2026-04-17 23:50 UTC): Autoscaler mis-scale event causing transient 503s. Scope: spike during synthetic load test. RCA: scale-down cooldown misconfigured, race with policy. Status: cooldown adjusted; tests green. Follow-up: add scale-safety floor in autoscaler config.

Proposed agenda (15-20 min):
1) Quick metrics + top-3 incidents recap (5 min)
2) Decide 2 operational priorities (10 min)
   - Candidate A: driver roll + node remediation plan for Dedicated pool (owner: Arjun)
   - Candidate B: cache-key rollout guardrails + canary + cache-warm job (owner: Marta)
   - Candidate C: autoscaler cooldown + safety floor config + test matrix (owner: Ethan)
3) Action assignment + deadlines (5 min)
4) Anything else / blockers (if time)

Decision criteria for prioritization:
- Reduces >30% of pages in last 30d for a single alert source OR prevents a high-severity incident from recurring.
- Work <= 8 dev-days to complete (or staged with immediate mitigation + follow-up).
- Minimal risk to customer traffic during change; prefer canaryed approach.

Draft action items (to record during meeting):
- Arjun: schedule Dedicated GPU driver updates for us-west-2, create maintenance windows doc, ETA 2026-04-26. (TODO add to ENGINFRA-2345)
- Marta: implement cache-rollout checklist and single-server canary; add cache-warm job; PR and rollout plan by 2026-04-23.
- Ethan: change autoscaler cooldown default, add safety floor, run 2 synthetic stress tests; PR by 2026-04-21, tests by 2026-04-24.
- Priya (me): follow up with CS on incidents A/B to confirm customer impact logging; update incident notes and comms draft by EOD 2026-04-19.
- On-call SRE: add a short-term alert to monitor KV eviction rate and driver stalls (runbook link in linked_artifacts) before changes land.

Notes/questions to bring up:
- Do we have a low-effort metric to show reduction in pages if we implement Candidate B? (e.g., expected cache hit rate delta)
- Can platform team add a simple per-node NVML watchdog to surface driver stalls earlier? (if yes, how long to prototype)
- Any dependent teams impacted by driver roll (release-engineering, infra)? Notify them earlier.

Runbook/comms checklist (for follow-up after decisions):
- Create short customer-facing postmortem if burn >10% SLO or >1 major customer impacted.
- Update runbooks for the specific alerts: model-serving-timeouts, kv-cache-evictions, autoscaler-throttles.
- Add test cases for canary routes in CI (small smoke harness).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the meeting tight — avoid deep technical dive, assign owners and timebox.
- Bring one slide with: trend charts + top 3 incident bullets + proposed choices.
- If time permits, quick retrospective on alert thresholds: are thresholds tuned to true user-impact?

End of scratchpad.
